# Block GrowthBook Adoption and Query Optimization
Date: 2026-11-17 | Duration: 42.41999816894531m

## Summary
Block is consolidating GrowthBook under Alyssa’s experimentation and LLM evaluation mandate, with enrollment, proxy-server use, and remote evaluation viewed as more strategic than dashboarding. Repeated exposure-to-fact-table joins may require separate processing for 50 or more experiments and could become more costly at larger scale. Proposed mitigations included shared processing, experiment-key and unit-ID partitioning, clustering, and separate warehouses for scheduled refreshes and ad hoc work; Block reported 61 timed-out queries costing $750 over seven days. A reusable user-metric-day rollup could support data-scientist analysis and meta-analysis, although funnel metrics require timestamp arrays and freshness, restatement, dependency, and cache-divergence risks remain. Block also needs legacy-metric cleanup, migration support, and potentially a fresh configuration. Luke planned follow-up guidance on partitioning, clustering, warehouse scheduling, pre-aggregation, and migration, with hands-on organizational support favored.

## Keywords
Experiment-data pipelines, Snowflake optimisation, Pre-aggregated tables, Metric restatement, Warehouse scaling, Legacy-metric migration

## Action Items
**Luke Sonnet**
Provide Block guidance on query clustering and partitioning (33:49)
Recommend Snowflake warehouse scaling and scheduling (33:49)
Present pre-aggregated user-day metric table opportunity (33:49)
Offer Block migration tool (36:52)
Share migration and legacy-metric cleanup guidance (39:35)
Share pre-aggregated table trade-offs (40:37)
